name: MAX40200AUK+T
title: MAX40200: micropower 1 A ideal diode, 1.5 V to 5.5 V, WLP and SOT-23
summary: A single ideal diode built on an internal p-channel MOSFET, passing up to 1 A from VDD (anode) to OUT (cathode) with a forward drop of 43 mV typ at 500 mA in WLP and 97 mV typ in SOT-23. It blocks reverse current like a diode, can be switched off through EN (then blocking up to 6 V either way), and shuts itself off when too hot. It runs from 1.5 V to 5.5 V on 7 µA typ quiescent current, over -40 °C to +125 °C, in a 0.73 mm × 0.73 mm 4-bump WLP or a 5-pin SOT-23; MAX40200AUK+T is the SOT-23 part.
key_figures: 43 mV typ, 89 mV max (WLP); 97 mV typ, 175 mV max (SOT)
7 µA typ, 18 µA max enabled; 0.7 µA typ disabled

circuits.title: Test setup: forward-biased condition
circuits.description: A supply VDD feeds the anode pin, with EN strapped to it so the device is on. An adjustable load resistor from OUT to ground sets IFORWARD; VFWD is taken between a terminal on VDD and a terminal on OUT, and an ammeter in the GND lead reads the ground or quiescent current.

circuits.title: Test setup: reverse-biased condition
circuits.description: One source holds the anode pin at VDD and a second drives OUT, both from ground, so OUT can be set above VDD. IANODE is the current in the VDD lead, ICATHODE the current in the OUT lead, and an ammeter in the GND lead reads the ground current. EN is brought out to set the enable state.

circuits.title: Diode ORing circuit 1
circuits.description: A wall adapter and a battery share one load. The adapter reaches the load through an ordinary diode D1; the battery reaches it through the MAX40200, which loses only tens of millivolts and stops current flowing back into the battery when the adapter voltage is higher. EN lets the battery path be switched off. A capacitor sits across the load at the output.
notes: The device needs at least 0.33 µF on OUT and on VDD for loop stability.

circuits.title: Diode ORing circuit 2
circuits.description: The load is split in two. The wall adapter feeds each half through its own diode, D1 to load A and D2 to load B. One battery feeds both halves, each through its own MAX40200, so each half can be switched off from the battery by its own EN line while still being fed by the adapter. Each output has a capacitor across its load.
notes: The device needs at least 0.33 µF on OUT and on VDD for loop stability.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: A battery powers a group of sub-circuits through one MAX40200. Driving EN low cuts power to all of them at once, giving power-down to circuits that have none of their own.

operation.text: The device behaves as a diode with a nearly constant forward drop instead of a normal diode's cut-in voltage of about 500 mV and logarithmic curve: about 45 mV at 500 mA. A normal diode's drop grows by about 60 mV for each tenfold rise in current. Past its rated current the device becomes resistive. It blocks reverse voltage like a diode. It is meant for switching between DC sources, not for rectifying AC; an inductively coupled supply still needs conventional rectifier diodes.

An internal p-channel MOSFET carries current from VDD to OUT. Its control circuit holds an 18 mV forward drop while forward-biased, and shuts the MOSFET off under reverse bias, when EN is low, or when the die passes the thermal protection threshold. The control circuit draws about 7 µA, which limits how fast it can turn the MOSFET on and off; switching it with EN takes about as long as switching it by forward or reverse bias.

EN high turns the device on and EN low turns it off; EN has an active pull-up. Off, it blocks up to 6 V above ground on either side, which lets it select between supplies or decide which sub-circuits receive power.

For loop stability at every load current, keep at least 0.33 µF on OUT and at least 0.33 µF on VDD. These capacitors also help the supply ride through surges. With a large output capacitor such as 10 µF, size the input capacitor near COUT/10 for the best transient response. The rated stable output capacitance is 0.3 µF to 100 µF.

Dissipation is VFWD × IFWD and grows with load because VFWD rises linearly with current; heavy loads of 500 mA to 1 A need care. The heat goes into the board, so the board temperature is the ambient. At a junction temperature of about +154 °C the device shuts off and restarts once it cools by the hysteresis (10 °C typ; 12 °C typ is also given), so an overloaded part cycles its output on and off. At TA = 125 °C the WLP part cycles with a period of tens of milliseconds and the SOT part hundreds. The WLP package handles heat better than the SOT-23.

In the ORing circuits the adapter path can use an ordinary diode since the adapter can afford its loss, while the battery path uses the MAX40200 and gives up only about 30 mV, lengthening run time between charges. A load that needs more current than one device carries can be split into sections, each fed by its own device and its own enable. Placing the device in a circuit's supply adds a power-down control to parts that lack one.
